title: WASSCE Technical Drawing: Complete Preparation
description: A full 10-module WASSCE Technical Drawing preparation course aligned to the WAEC syllabus: drawing instruments & skills, geometrical constructions, orthographic projection, isometric & oblique drawing, sectional views & development, building & mechanical drawing, CAD basics, examination practice, revision, and a full mock examination with a Certificate of Completion.
outcomes: Understand the WAEC Technical Drawing exam structure and marking scheme
Use drawing instruments and apply line, lettering and dimensioning standards
Perform geometrical constructions: bisections, polygons, tangents and loci
Produce orthographic projections (first- and third-angle) and read drawings
Create isometric, oblique, sectional and development drawings
Interpret building/mechanical drawings and use CAD basics
about: This is the complete TIH WASSCE Technical Drawing preparation course, organised into ten modules aligned to the WAEC Technical Drawing syllabus and examination structure (objective and practical drawing).

Every content lesson has a video and printable notes with worked construction steps and drawing conventions; downloadable resources include drawing sheets, engineering templates and instrument/CAD guides. The course ends with a full mock examination and a Certificate of Completion.

Technical Drawing is highly practical — you must draw regularly with proper instruments. Use this course together with the official WAEC syllabus, your teacher’s guidance and WAEC past questions for best results.
requirements: A phone or computer with internet
Drawing instruments (board/T-square, set squares, compass, scale rule)
Access to CAD software for the CAD module (optional)

Bisecting Lines and Angles

This lesson builds geometrical constructions through clear method, worked construction steps and timed drawing practice. Watch the video, study the notes and worked steps, then complete the two drawing exercises before the short quiz.

Key points

  • Learn the method/convention for Bisecting Lines and Angles and how WAEC tests it in the drawing paper.
  • Follow the construction step by step, keeping instruments sharp and lines to standard.
  • Practise with past-question-style items, drawing accurately to scale and leaving construction lines.

📥 Guide: Geometrical Constructions

  • Bisecting: use equal arcs from both ends to bisect a line or angle.
  • Polygons: construct regular polygons in/around a circle.
  • Tangents: a tangent touches a circle at 90° to the radius.
  • Loci: the path traced by a point moving under a rule.
  • Always leave your construction arcs visible — examiners award method marks.

options: Objective questions and practical drawing papers
questions.explanation: It has objective and practical drawing components.

questions.question: In the drawing paper, marks are earned mainly for:
options: Accuracy, correct method and neatness to standard
questions.explanation: Accuracy, method and neat standard work score marks.

questions.question: You should leave construction lines on a geometry drawing because they:
options: Show your method and earn marks
questions.explanation: Construction lines show the method examiners reward.

questions.question: A good study strategy for technical drawing is to:
options: Practise drawings regularly under timed conditions
questions.explanation: Regular timed drawing practice builds accuracy and speed.

questions.question: The T-square is used mainly to draw:
questions.explanation: The T-square draws horizontal lines and guides set squares.

questions.question: Set squares commonly provide angles of:
questions.explanation: The two set squares give 45° and 30°/60°.

questions.question: A compass is used to draw:
questions.explanation: A compass draws circles and arcs.

questions.question: Hidden edges of an object are shown with:
questions.explanation: Hidden detail is drawn with dashed lines.

questions.question: Centre lines are drawn as:
questions.explanation: Centre lines use a chain-line convention.

questions.question: Dividers are used to:
questions.explanation: Dividers transfer and step off measurements.

questions.question: To bisect a line you draw equal arcs from:
questions.explanation: Equal arcs from both ends give the perpendicular bisector.

questions.question: A tangent to a circle meets the radius at:
questions.explanation: A tangent is perpendicular (90°) to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.question: A regular hexagon has how many equal sides?
questions.explanation: A hexagon has 6 equal sides.
